task.title: Editing a Target Database Profile
task.shortdesc: To edit an existing database profile, do the following:

step.cmd: Click Databases in the main menu. A list of existing database profiles will be displayed.
Click name of the required database in the list.
Click Add Interface to add a new database interface and specify hostname, port number, database keys and IP version (also SID or service name for Oracle Database). Click Save to apply new settings.
To add a new proxy for the database, do the following:

substep.cmd: Select a network interface for the database in the Interface drop-down list.
Select an application server (node) on which to open a proxy in the Server drop-down list.
Select new database host in the Host drop-down list.
Specify port number for the application's proxy in the Port text field.
Check the Enabled check box to activate the proxy.
Check the Separate Message Handler and Audit Journal check box for corresponding settings.

ul.li: Separate Message Handler check box: When checked, a separate Message handler is created for the proxy. You can specify the number of threads for the Message handler.
Separate Audit Journal check box: When checked, a separate Audit journal is created for the proxy. You can specify the number of threads for the Audit journal.

substep.cmd: Click Save to apply new settings.

step.cmd: To add a new sniffer to the database, do the following:

substep.cmd: Select a required network interface in the Instance Interface drop-down list. An Interface has an IP address and a port number on which a target server is listening. The application opens a proxy or a sniffer on an interface. A database instance can include several interfaces.
Select an application server (node) to open a sniffer on, in the Server drop-down list.
Select a required network device (network adapter) in the Device drop-down list.
Specify Sniffer keys if necessary. Sniffer key is a database server's private SSL key. It is used to decrypt the traffic flowing between the client and the database.
Check the Enabled check box to activate a current sniffer.
Click Save to apply new settings.

info.note: If the database server, database client and the firewall are installed on the same Windows-powered local machine, the application sniffer will not be able to capture network traffic.

step.cmd: Click Actions → Update Metadata to update the database's metadata.

info.note: Database's metadata contains information about the database structure, tables' properties, etc. The application creates database metadata copy in the dictionary.db file which is located within the program installation folder, and uses it for processing of the database's traffic. The application keeps metadata copy up to date automatically, but if some serious error occurs or the database were updated directly (bypassing the application), you should update the metadata manually by clicking Update Metadata. If you update your target database often directly, we recommend you to configure a Periodic Metadata Update task and run it as often as you update the database (refer to subs, ).

step.cmd: Click Actions → Test Connections to test a connection between the application server and the target database. Enter required credentials in the Connection to Database window.
